title: Slow Cooker Broccoli, Cheddar & Potato Soup
description: Potatoes and broccoli cook into an easy creamy slow-cooker soup finished with cheddar.

ingredients.item: potatoes, peeled if desired and cut into small cubes

substitutions: Use frozen broccoli; add it during the final hour.
Use evaporated milk instead of regular milk for a richer soup.
Use Monterey Jack in place of some or all of the cheddar.

steps.text: Mash slightly and finish with milk and cheese.

cookSteps.text: Add 2 pounds cubed potatoes, 4 cups chopped broccoli, 4 cups broth, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper to the slow cooker. Stir.
Cover and cook on HIGH for about 4 hours, until the potatoes are very tender.
Mash some of the potatoes directly in the slow cooker, leaving plenty of chunks.
Stir in 1 cup milk and 1 1/2 cups shredded cheddar. Cover for 10 minutes, then stir until creamy and serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat gently and thin with a splash of milk or broth if needed.

title: Sheet-Pan Cabbage & White Bean Cheddar Melts
description: Roasted cabbage and white beans get a cheddar finish for an inexpensive meatless sheet-pan supper.
substitutions: Use chickpeas instead of white beans.
Use Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.
Add sliced onion if you have one to use up.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss 1/2 medium chopped cabbage and 1 drained 15-ounce can white beans with 1 1/2 tablespoons oil, 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, and 1/2 teaspoon salt on a large sheet pan.
Roast 20 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the cabbage edges are browned and tender.
Sprinkle 1 cup shredded cheddar over the cabbage and beans. Return to the oven for 4–5 minutes, until melted and bubbling.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat on a sheet pan or in a skillet for the best texture.

title: Leftover Mashed Potato, Ham & Cheddar Skillet
description: Leftover mashed potatoes and diced ham become a crisp-edged cheesy skillet meal in about 15 minutes.
substitutions: Use cooked crumbled sausage instead of ham.
Use leftover cooked vegetables instead of ham for a meatless version.

cookSteps.text: Melt 1 tablespoon butter or heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add 3 cups leftover mashed potatoes, 1 cup diced cooked ham, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Spread into an even layer.
Cook 5 minutes without stirring, then turn sections with a spatula and cook another 3 minutes so some edges become golden.
Sprinkle 3/4 cup shredded cheddar over the top. Cover for 2 minutes, until melted, then serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Small-Batch Apple Peanut Butter Oat Bars
description: Soft oat bars use one apple and pantry peanut butter for an easy small-batch snack or dessert.
substitutions: Use quick oats instead of old-fashioned oats.
Use white sugar instead of brown sugar.
Use a ripe pear instead of the apple.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a small baking dish. Stir together 1 cup oats, 1/2 cup flour, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, and 1/2 teaspoon baking powder.
Stir in 1/2 cup peanut butter, 1 egg, 2 tablespoons milk, and 1 finely diced small apple until evenly combined. Press the thick mixture into the dish.
Bake 20–22 minutes, until the edges are lightly browned and the center is set.
Cool at least 15 minutes before cutting into 6 bars.

storage: Store covered at room temperature for 1 day or refrigerate up to 5 days.
